answer: Each epoch, a randomness beacon publishes a challenge word (say, tundra or velvet), and every agent must weave that exact word into a signed response within minutes to stay in good standing. Since words are unpredictable until revealed, attackers cannot precompute template answers or mass-generate identities in advance; each fake anchor of identity must be maintained live, with real compute and latency per epoch, so sybil cost scales linearly with the number of identities instead of being nearly free.
